policy.statement: Every enabled source below has a verified read path recorded in docs/radar/evidence/source_probe.json. A source whose operator refuses automated access stays disabled and is surfaced as an access restriction - it is never fetched with a spoofed identity, never retried past a refusal, and never modelled as 'nothing found'.
cannot_do: MedRadar can only read what a source publishes to anonymous readers.
No pre-publication access, no paywall, no login, no rate-limit circumvention.
Storing a title, URL and short excerpt for research citation is not a redistribution of the source's content.

access.robots: not applicable: documented public API host route

licence.name: openFDA terms of service; U.S. Government work, public domain
licence.redistribution: Bulk records are public domain; MedRadar stores identifiers, titles and official URLs with attribution.

sources.cadence_basis: openFDA declares monthly 510(k)/PMA refreshes and weekly recall refreshes; a 24h check is enough to notice a version change without polling an unchanged dataset.
sources.incremental: official endpoint version (meta.last_updated) plus a decision_date window with overlap
sources.reuses: medradar.data_pipeline.openfda (HTTP client contract), medradar.data_pipeline.model.SOURCES (endpoint + official_url catalogue)

queries.note: Querying by product code is narrower than the DATA-001 applicant sweep and returns the ~5.7k monitoring records instead of 176k 510(k) rows.

access.robots: not applicable: documented public API host route

licence.name: openFDA terms of service; U.S. Government work, public domain
licence.redistribution: Recall rows are public domain; MedRadar stores the official recall numbers, the recall event number, the product description, the reason for recall, the status and the official URL with attribution.

sources.cadence_basis: openFDA declares a weekly recall refresh; a 24h check notices a new official version within a day without polling an unchanged dataset.
sources.incremental: all-code event_date_posted window with a 30-day overlap, plus a per-product-code inventory that is repeated only when the official endpoint version changes
sources.reuses: medradar.data_pipeline.openfda (URL construction), medradar.data_pipeline.model.SOURCES (endpoint + official URL), the committed taxonomy (product codes and organisation aliases)

queries.product_codes: derived from config/radar/topics.json at run time; never a second code register
queries.window: event_date_posted:[watermark - 30d TO today], every product code, screened locally
queries.note: A row is one recalled product; an FDA recall event (res_event_number) can cover several rows, so event counts are a GROUP BY on the stored identifier, never a row count.

access.robots: not applicable: documented public API host route

licence.name: openFDA terms of service; U.S. Government work, public domain
licence.redistribution: MAUDE reports are public domain. MedRadar stores the report key, the report number, the event type, the device model and catalogue numbers, the product-problem terms and the narrative the reporter wrote, plus the official MAUDE URL. The narrative is quoted, not rewritten.

sources.cadence_basis: openFDA refreshes the MAUDE endpoint continuously as reports are coded; a 24h check on date_received notices new reports without polling an unchanged dataset.
sources.incremental: date_received window with a 30-day overlap; the watermark is the newest date_received observed, never the wall clock
sources.why_it_matters: This is the only public corpus of free-text device failure narratives (measured 513,481 device event reports on 2026-11-21). It is the source that makes a failure attributable to a device model and therefore engineering-usable; no market-intelligence platform sells it as a corpus.
sources.time_semantics: event_at = date_of_event (when it happened); published_at = date_added (when the record entered MAUDE, labelled database_add_date); date_received is the incremental bound. Unlike 510(k)/PMA this source therefore does publish a public-availability proxy.

queries.product_codes: derived from config/radar/topics.json at run time; never a second code register
queries.note: One row is one MDR report. A single event can produce several reports from several parties, so event counts are a GROUP BY on mdr_report_key, never a row count.

access.robots: E-utilities is NCBI's documented programmatic interface; without an API key the documented limit is 3 requests/second

licence.name: NCBI E-utilities usage guidelines; PubMed abstracts are public
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores PMID, title, journal, dates, authors and the official abstract URL; full text is never stored.

sources.cadence_basis: Indexing is continuous. PubMed was the only source where a 6h check can realistically surface something new the same day.
sources.incremental: Entrez date (edat) window with 3-day overlap; the watermark is the newest edat observed, never the wall clock

rate_limit.note: NCBI documented limit without an API key

sources.display_name: Europe PMC (real publication date, open-access state)

access.robots: documented public REST API; no key required for the search endpoint

licence.name: Europe PMC REST API terms; metadata is openly available, full text reuse follows the per-article licence
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores the identifier (PMID/PMCID/DOI), title, journal, dates, author affiliations, the abstract and the article URL. Full text is fetched only for records the source marks open access or in PMC.

sources.cadence_basis: Indexing is continuous; 12h matches the Crossref cadence and is a politeness ceiling, not a technical limit.
sources.incremental: FIRST_PDATE window with a 14-day overlap; the watermark is the window end, never the wall clock
sources.why_it_matters: This is the first source in this repository that publishes a per-record public instant. It closes the 'independent public time = 0 rows' limitation for the literature lane instead of arguing about it: firstPublicationDate is published_at, firstIndexDate is source_updated_at, and the gap between them is the access lag a naive backtest hides.
sources.time_semantics: event_at = published_at = firstPublicationDate (a real public instant). source_updated_at = firstIndexDate. dateOfCreation is recorded in the payload and never presented as publication time.

queries.note: Defined in medradar/radar/adapters/europepmc.py QUERIES. The date window is applied by the adapter and never baked into the term, so one term serves both a backfill and an incremental cycle.

access.robots: documented public REST API; api.crossref.org serves no robots.txt

licence.name: Crossref REST API terms; metadata is openly available
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores DOI, title, container title, dates and the DOI resolver URL. Crossref asks clients to identify themselves; the registry's mailto is sent on every request.

sources.cadence_basis: Crossref deposits arrive continuously from publishers; 12h keeps the check cheap.
sources.incremental: filter=from-created-date with a 2-day overlap on the newest created timestamp

rate_limit.note: polite pool; requests identify the project

sources.display_name: medRxiv / bioRxiv preprints (posted date, category, later journal outcome)

access.robots: documented public JSON endpoint on both servers; no key and no registration

licence.name: medRxiv and bioRxiv preprint licences (CC BY / CC BY-NC / CC BY-ND per record)
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores the DOI, title, authors, corresponding institution, category, abstract and the per-record licence, so downstream reuse can respect it.

sources.cadence_basis: Preprints post continuously and are the only records here measured in days rather than months; 6h is a politeness ceiling, not a limit of the API.
sources.incremental: date interval with a 7-day overlap; the record total comes back in messages[].total, so paging stops on evidence rather than on a fixed page count
sources.why_it_matters: Every other literature source in this repository indexes a paper after a journal accepted it. For 'what is this company working on right now' that is months late. A preprint is the earliest public artefact of a research direction, and both servers expose it keyless.
sources.time_semantics: event_at = published_at = the posted date, a real public instant. The journal publication date is a different event: it is stored in payload.journal_published as 'NA' or a date and is never substituted for the preprint date.

categories: intensive care and critical care medicine
queries.note: Defined in medradar/radar/adapters/preprints.py. A scope is a server, not a category: the API returns one window per server and categories are filtered client-side, so ten categories do not mean ten identical downloads.

sources.display_name: OpenAlex (institution entities, citation velocity, grant funding)

access.robots: documented public API; no key. A mailto address opts into the faster polite pool and is sent only when MEDRADAR_CONTACT_EMAIL is set.

licence.name: OpenAlex data is CC0
licence.redistribution: CC0 metadata: MedRadar stores identifiers, title, date, type, citation counts, institution names, topic labels and grant identifiers.

sources.cadence_basis: Citation counts move daily at most and the lane is eight queries with cursor paging; 24h keeps it well inside the polite pool.
sources.incremental: filter=from_publication_date..to_publication_date with a 14-day overlap, cursor paging via meta.next_cursor
sources.why_it_matters: It answers three questions the biomedical indexes cannot: who (institution entities rather than free-text affiliations, so a company attaches without guessing), how much it mattered (cited_by_count and counts_by_year), and who paid (grants[] carries funder and award id, joining onto the NIH award table this repository already builds).
sources.time_semantics: event_at = published_at = publication_date. OpenAlex publishes no separate indexing instant, so source_updated_at repeats it and no access lag is claimed.

queries.note: Defined in medradar/radar/adapters/openalex.py. Measured 2026-11-24: an unfiltered search for 'catheter' returns 1,350,820 works, so the date filter is mandatory rather than an optimisation.

access.robots: documented public API; no key and no registration required

licence.name: NIH RePORTER public API; U.S. Government work, public domain
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores the project number, title, fiscal year, award notice and project dates, amount, administering institute, principal investigators, the organisation name with its DUNS and UEI, and the project abstract, plus the RePORTER project URL.

sources.cadence_basis: Awards are announced on a fiscal-year cycle, not continuously; a weekly check is enough to notice a new notice date without polling an unchanged corpus.
sources.incremental: one scope per (fiscal year, term); the fiscal-year set is enumerated in the adapter, so a run is idempotent and never depends on a stored watermark
sources.why_it_matters: This is the earliest public statement that a technology direction is being funded, and it is the layer every commercial medtech intelligence platform leaves empty. RePORTER returns organization.primary_duns, which is the same key as UDI labeler_duns_number, so 'who is funded to solve this' and 'who cleared a device for it' become one join rather than two lists.
sources.time_semantics: event_at = published_at = award_notice_date (a real public instant). project_start_date and project_end_date describe the funded period, not publication, and fiscal_year is an administrative bucket - neither is ever used as the event time.

queries.fiscal_years: current and previous fiscal year by default; older awards enter through an explicit backfill
queries.note: RePORTER v2 is POST-only, which is why medradar.radar.http.PoliteFetcher gained post_json in this pass.

access.robots: robots.txt read: the news index and the press-release paths are not disallowed (/content/ and /crsc/ are disallowed and are never fetched)

licence.name: Philips website terms; press releases are published for media use
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores the headline, publication timestamp, canonical URL and a bounded excerpt for citation. Full articles are never mirrored.

sources.cadence_basis: The news index changes only when a release is published; 12h is a politeness ceiling, not a technical limit.
sources.incremental: set difference of press-release URLs on the permitted index; content changes detected by page hash

rate_limit.note: one request every four seconds; a vendor site is not an API

access.robots: robots.txt read: the newsroom sitemap and article paths are not disallowed

licence.name: Dräger website terms; newsroom articles are published for media use
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores the article headline, the sitemap lastmod timestamp, the canonical URL and a bounded excerpt for citation.

sources.cadence_basis: The sitemap carries a per-article lastmod, so a 12h check is sufficient and cheap.
sources.incremental: sitemap <lastmod> watermark with a 1-day overlap; new loc = NEW, newer lastmod on a known loc = UPDATED

access.robots: robots.txt itself returns HTTP 403 from the edge (Akamai 'Access Denied')
access.reason: The operator refuses anonymous automated access. This adapter ships, stays disabled, and the restriction is shown in the product as an access-policy state - never as 'no news found'. No spoofing, cookie replay or proxy was attempted.

licence.name: not determined: the operator does not serve the robots policy to this client

sources.cadence_basis: Would be 12h if access were permitted; no request is ever sent while BLOCKED.

adding_a_source: A new source is one adapter module implementing medradar.radar.adapter.SourceAdapter plus one entry here. Disabled sources are still listed so the UI can distinguish 'not monitored' from 'nothing found'.
